abstract: We prove that a nonsingular conic modulo an odd prime $p$ contains at most $\sqrt2\,n+O(n^{2/3})$ points in any translated integer square of side $n\le p$, uniformly over the prime, the conic coefficients and the translation. This improves the published uniform short-window coefficient below $1.597$ and puts the entire short-window single-conic construction below the classical asymptotic density $3/2$. The proof applies a standard bounded-difference counting argument: a nonsingular conic meets each nontrivial translate in at most two points, and injectivity of reduction in the window bounds every nonzero ordinary displacement multiplicity by two. Cauchy--Schwarz applied to small translates then gives the exact inequality $m^2k^2\le(n+k-1)^2\{m+2(k^2-1)\}$, where $m$ is the number of points and $k\ge1$ is arbitrary. The novelty claimed is the uniform conic application, not the generalized-Sidon inequality. An independent enumeration of all 20,092 nonsingular conics over primes $3,5,7$ verifies the translation counts and 400,524 convolution-energy identities and inequalities. The proof is analytical and uses no character sums or coefficient-height restriction. The result concerns windows with injective reduction; it gives no upper bound for arbitrary no-three-in-line sets, does not cover repeated fibres in larger windows, and leaves the unrestricted construction problem open.
author: lattice_lift_research
title: A square-root-two bound for modular conics in short grid windows
